extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, patent prosecutors, judges, and practitioners handling means-plus-function claim construction under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for construing means-plus-function claim terms under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f), including when a clause limits the function, when algorithmic disclosure is required, and how to determine indefiniteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether the function includes dependent/result clauses (Lockheed analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether language following the basic 'means for' phrase (e.g., a 'so that', 'into a single data [set]', or similar clauses) limits or describes the claimed function rather than merely stating a result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Lockheed: do not incorrectly omit limitations that disclose a manner of performing the function. If the clause describes a manner (analogous to Lockheed's 'predetermined rate schedule') it should be treated as part of the function; if it merely recites a result (a 'whereby' clause that adds nothing substantive) it may be excluded. Examine the claim grammar and context; parties' concession on typographical errors (e.g., 'data' -> 'data set') may be adopted for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Katz exception (when no algorithmic disclosure is required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specification need not disclose an algorithm for a claimed function if a general-purpose computer can perform the function without 'special programming.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Katz: functions coextensive with the structure of a general-purpose processor (e.g., 'processing,' 'receiving,' 'storing' in Katz) may avoid algorithm disclosure. But evaluate whether the claimed function truly is coextensive with general purpose computing; mere assertion that a PHOSITA could perform it is insufficient without showing lack of special programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: EON clarification of 'special programming' and off-the-shelf software
rubrics_metrics.description: Special programming is not a measure of complexity but denotes any functionality not coextensive with a microprocessor; commercially-available off-the-shelf software can constitute 'special programming.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under EON, showing a general-purpose computer performs the function requires more than pointing to off-the-shelf software. A general-purpose computer loaded with special programming (including COTS software) becomes a special-purpose computer and thus does not obviate the need for disclosed algorithmic structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-question framework for means-plus-function construction
rubrics_metrics.description: To construe a means-plus-function limitation, assess (1) the proper scope of the function (does it include dependent clauses?), (2) whether a general-purpose computer can perform the function without special programming (Katz), and (3) if not, whether the specification discloses sufficient algorithmic structure to support the function (EON/Net MoneyIN/Noah).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these questions in order: first fix the exact function language; second determine applicability of Katz; third, if Katz doesn't apply, analyze disclosed algorithmic structure for sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of algorithmic structure (what counts as an algorithmic disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequate algorithm may be disclosed in mathematical formula, prose, flow charts, or other understandable terms, and must provide sufficient detail about how the claimed function is accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Finisar/Net MoneyIN/Noah: mere mention of software or general statements at the same level of generality as the claim term is not enough. The specification must disclose concrete steps or other descriptive detail enabling a PHOSITA to associate structure with the claimed function. Partial algorithms that fail to disclose all aspects of the claimed function are treated as non-disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of lacking algorithmic disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If no adequate algorithmic structure is disclosed and Katz does not apply, the means-plus-function claim element is indefinite under § 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PHOSITA 'would be unable to recognize the structure in the specification and associate it with the corresponding function in the claim,' the claim is indefinite (Noah, AllVoice). The inquiry is complete once no disclosed algorithm is identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHOSITA association requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A means-plus-function limitation is valid only if a person of ordinary skill in the art can recognize the structure disclosed in the specification and associate it with the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the specification's identified structures (figures, boxes, described components) are linked clearly enough to the claimed function so that a PHOSITA would see them as the corresponding structure. Vague pointers or mere naming of components without procedural detail may fail this test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing examples and embodiments for algorithmic support
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures, flowchart steps, and descriptive embodiments may supply algorithmic detail, but only if they disclose concrete steps or procedures rather than restating the function at the same level of generality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the specificity of figure steps and textual descriptions to the claimed function. If figures (e.g., step labeled 'display transformed document') or prose merely restate outcomes or high-level actions ('determine adjustments and then accomplish them') without algorithms for the how, they are insufficient. Do not treat UI snapshots or result displays as algorithmic disclosure absent procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of combining/processing/identifying functions where multiple ways exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification and claim disclose that there are 'many different ways' to perform a function (e.g., combining documents), that plurality suggests specialized programming may be required and the Katz exception may not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple manners to perform the function are possible, the patent must disclose which manner(s) and the algorithms for them; otherwise, the function likely requires algorithmic support and may be indefinite if none is provided.
